The truth is nothing ever changes in the market, longevity and emotional discipline are the main issues to tackle. 
Bubbles will constantly inflate and bust and the opportunity to earn is always there. 

Was it “simpler” to win in let’s say the 70s commodity cycles, when trading with moving averages and basic trend following technicals gave you an edge? Sure. But the books outlining such strategies didn’t exist, people thought of these concepts, which were novel at the time, on their own. seykota esque “TA” as a school of thought was voodoo witchcraft. These simple strats may appear primitive now but he made millions on them. 

Sure the avg participant is more knowledgeable about technicals and tooling now, but resources to learn this exist and are easily accessible, you don’t have to create these tools yourself. This doesn’t mean the market is harder now. The tools giving traders a real edge today are being created right now by forward thinkers, and in 20 years there will be resources outlining how these work and they will appear primitive again. 

Longevity is everything. “It was easier to hit big returns early in crypto, it was less sophisticated”. Sure, but x person would’ve sold btc early, similarly to how they missed or fumbled the trumpcoin launch or countless other opportunities. Or they’ll blow up later. The ability to earn exists in markets forever. 

Nothing changes, the thing that kills the speculator is always himself.

Here is a throwback to when I’d actually explain concepts. Since I bitched about bad content, I’ll do an educational post for today.

Wrote a thing back in the day about how correlation is misapplied as a concept by many traders. 

“Correlation is not static, neither in strength nor even direction”. 

Example given was during Covid when we had massive printing, commodities like crude would trend up together with risk assets. Positive correlation. 

After, when policy shifted to tightening and rate hikes, crude became inversely correlated to equities/risk. Because higher commodity prices meant greater inflation which meant more hikes and tightening required because economy ran hot. Bad for risk, inverse correlation. Equities low in June coincided with crude top. 

Complete correlation flip directionally. 

Attempting to apply correlation without understanding fundamental backdrop is worthless, similar to how many are always trying to make it so that dxy up = risk assets down. 

The cause is important.
